status: Exploratory amendment after the declared rounding test exposed certificate discontinuities; before high-precision roots or revised rankings are computed.
trigger: Rounding coefficients to ten significant digits changed individual block/pair-cell scores by several points despite common accepted roots moving by less than 1e-7 inhibition points.
hypothesis: Near-asymptote cancellation in the inverse-effect certificate, rather than large movement of the mathematical root, accounts for some apparent root-status instability.
scope: Historical fallback cases where the double-precision forward solver finds a same-direction bracketed root but the inverse-equation residual exceeds 1e-8 or the strict-domain test fails. Existing 14,197-case results remain the primary historical correction.
method: An independent 100-decimal-digit bisection in common-effect coordinates over the joint effect interval, parameterized by a logit coordinate in [-200,200]. Require strict interior membership and inverse-equation residual <1e-30 at high precision. Opposite/flat curves and no bracket remain unresolved. Recheck 100 seed-selected well-certified controls. Compare unchanged coefficients and ten-significant-digit coefficients.
primary_metric: Count of double-precision failures with a high-precision-certified root, and maximum change of certified expected response after rounding.
secondary: Top-5% turnover using high-precision recovery in addition to the original valid-root correction; retain the original fallback and clipping conventions for unresolved cases. Report numerical stability separately from experimental validity.
decision: Attribute a certification discontinuity only when both high-precision roots satisfy the equation, move by less than 1e-3 inhibition points, and the double-precision accept/reject outcome differs. No claim of biological ranking improvement follows.
negative_result: Failure to certify at higher precision leaves a case unresolved; it must not be counted as a numerical artifact merely because a forward solver reports a boundary value.
